science_guardrail: IMPORTANT REVISION (2026-10-22): Do NOT key bushy versus broomsedge as simple 'hairy sheaths = glomeratum, hairless = virginicum'. The 2015 Texas Hill Country key describes hair on the distinct/open bushy sheath margins and generally entire broomsedge margins, sometimes with cilia on the outer edge. However Missouri, Texas A&M and Oklahoma sources explicitly show or describe broomsedge sheath or leaf-base hairs too. Species, growth stage, which margin is imaged, and geographic treatment can change the apparent difference. Inspect actual UPPER sheath shape and both separated margins on the SAME confirmed plant; treat hairs as one supporting character only. Big mature flowering architecture and measured rames/spikelets remain needed for confident separation.
needs_next: Leaf/sheath micro PHOTO gap: need matched correctly determined living Texas specimens, one photo to prove inner opened SHEATH margin and a second to prove outer SHEATH margin, then the true collar/ligule and ruler. Existing USGS broomsedge leaf/stem photos show some hairs near the sheath, but neither is yet proven to show both identifiable margins with enough resolution. University/extension photos with unclear public reuse rights must not be installed.
